genesis.24.p1.b1.text: By now Abraham was old and well along in years, and the LORD had blessed him in every way.

genesis.24.p1.b2.text: and I will have you swear by the LORD, the God of heaven and the God of earth, that you will not take a wife for my son from the daughters of the Canaanites among whom I am dwelling, but will go to my country and my kindred to take a wife for my son Isaac.”

genesis.24.p1.b3.text: What if the woman is unwilling to follow me to this land? Shall I then take your son back to the land from which you came?

genesis.24.p1.b4.text: Make sure that you do not take my son back there. … He will send His angel before you so that you can take a wife for my son from there.

genesis.24.p1.b5.text: So the servant placed his hand under the thigh of his master Abraham and swore an oath to him concerning this matter.

genesis.24.p2.b6.text: Then the servant took ten of his master’s camels … And he set out for Nahor’s hometown in Aram-naharaim.

genesis.24.p2.b7.text: As evening approached … at the time when the women went out to draw water.

genesis.24.p2.b8.text: O LORD, God of my master Abraham, … please grant me success today, and show kindness to my master Abraham.

genesis.24.p2.b9.text: … ‘Drink, and I will water your camels as well’—let her be the one You have appointed for Your servant Isaac.

genesis.24.p3.b10.text: Before the servant had finished praying, Rebekah came out with her jar on her shoulder.

genesis.24.p3.b11.text: Now the girl was very beautiful, … She went down to the spring, filled her jar, and came up again.

genesis.24.p3.b12.text: Please let me have a little water from your jar.

genesis.24.p4.b14.text: I will also draw water for your camels, until they have had enough to drink.

genesis.24.p4.b15.text: And she quickly emptied her jar into the trough …

genesis.24.p4.b16.text: Meanwhile, the man watched her silently to see whether or not the LORD had made his journey a success.

genesis.24.p4.b17.text: … and ran back to the well to draw water, until she had drawn water for all his camels.

genesis.24.p5.b18.text: And after the camels had finished drinking, he took out a gold ring … and two gold bracelets …

genesis.24.p5.b19.text: Whose daughter are you? … Please tell me, is there room in your father’s house for us to spend the night?

genesis.24.p5.b20.text: I am the daughter of Bethuel, the son that Milcah bore to Nahor. … We have plenty of straw and feed, as well as a place for you to spend the night.

genesis.24.p5.b21.text: Blessed be the LORD, the God of my master Abraham, who has not withheld His kindness and faithfulness from my master. As for me, the LORD has led me on the journey to the house of my master’s relatives.

genesis.24.p6.b22.text: The girl ran and told her mother’s household about these things.

genesis.24.p6.b23.text: Now Rebekah had a brother named Laban, and he rushed out to the man at the spring.

genesis.24.p6.b24.text: Come, you who are blessed by the LORD, … Why are you standing out here?

genesis.24.p6.b25.text: I will not eat until I have told you what I came to say.

genesis.24.p7.b28.text: The LORD has greatly blessed my master, and he has become rich. … and my master has given him everything he owns.

genesis.24.p7.b29.text: but you shall go to my father’s house and to my kindred to take a wife for my son.’

genesis.24.p7.b30.text: Then I asked my master, ‘What if the woman will not come back with me?’

genesis.24.p8.b31.text: So when I came to the spring today, I prayed: O LORD, God of my master Abraham, if only You would make my journey a success!

genesis.24.p8.b32.text: Drink, and I will water your camels as well.

genesis.24.p8.b33.text: So I drank, and she also watered the camels.

genesis.24.p8.b34.text: Now if you will show kindness and faithfulness to my master, tell me; but if not, let me know, so that I may go elsewhere.”

genesis.24.p9.b35.text: This is from the LORD; we have no choice in the matter. Rebekah is here before you. Take her and go, …

genesis.24.p9.b36.text: When Abraham’s servant heard their words, he bowed down to the ground before the LORD.

genesis.24.p9.b37.text: Then he brought out jewels of silver and gold, and articles of clothing, and he gave them to Rebekah. He also gave precious gifts to her brother and her mother.

genesis.24.p9.b38.text: … and spent the night there. When they got up the next morning, …

genesis.24.p9.b39.text: Send me on my way to my master.

genesis.24.p10.b40.text: Let the girl remain with us ten days or so. After that, she may go.

genesis.24.p10.b41.text: Do not delay me, … Send me on my way so that I may go to my master.

genesis.24.p10.b42.text: Will you go with this man?

genesis.24.p11.b44.text: Our sister, may you become the mother of thousands upon thousands. May your offspring possess the gates of their enemies.

genesis.24.p11.b45.text: So they sent their sister Rebekah on her way, along with her nurse and Abraham’s servant and his men.

genesis.24.p11.b46.text: Then Rebekah and her servant girls got ready, mounted the camels, and followed the man. So the servant took Rebekah and left.

genesis.24.p12.b47.text: Now Isaac had just returned from Beer-lahai-roi, for he was living in the Negev.

genesis.24.p12.b48.text: Early in the evening, Isaac went out to the field to meditate, …

genesis.24.p12.b49.text: … and looking up, he saw the camels approaching.

genesis.24.p13.b50.text: And when Rebekah looked up and saw Isaac, she got down from her camel

genesis.24.p13.b51.text: Who is that man in the field coming to meet us?

genesis.24.p13.b53.text: So she took her veil and covered herself.

genesis.24.p14.b54.text: Then the servant told Isaac all that he had done.

genesis.24.p14.b55.text: And Isaac brought her into the tent of his mother Sarah

genesis.24.p14.b56.text: and took Rebekah as his wife. And Isaac loved her and was comforted after his mother’s death.
